clue.text: Close to backing second treaty? Drinks to round things off

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near or close to

indicators.note: backing sends the two following pieces backwards, read from right to left

parts.note: a pact is a treaty or formal agreement

explanation.surface: A diplomat wonders whether a fresh treaty is near, then suggests a round of drinks to finish the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the second-plus-treaty pair only; 'Close to' supplies the opening synonym, not a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightcaps are the last drinks taken before bed, rounding off the evening.

clue.text: Name getting attention of immediate family

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A name catches the notice of someone's closest relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Near relations are close kin, so near describes someone of the immediate family.

clue.text: Government, making statement, on the way out

parts.note: uttering is speaking, making a statement

explanation.surface: A government still issuing announcements even as it is about to fall from power.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttering candle flickers as it burns down, so the word figuratively means fading or dying away.

clue.text: Rare element: description encompassing bismuth and uranium

indicators.note: encompassing means the word for description wraps round the two element symbols

parts.note: a term is a word or expression used to describe something
Bi is the chemical symbol for bismuth
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: the label for a rare element happens to contain two other elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Terbium is one of the lanthanides, the so-called rare-earth metals.

clue.text: Sign of agreement about fellows in it produces fellow-feeling

indicators.note: about tells us the sign of agreement goes around the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: ay (aye) is a word saying yes
F is an abbreviation for fellow, so FF is fellows
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nodding along with colleagues breeds a sense of comradeship.
explanation.definitionFit: Affinity is a natural liking or sympathy between people, a sense of kinship.

clue.text: Fight over club drug is an embarrassing event

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the fight word above the drug letter

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A brawl at a nightclub over drugs makes for a humiliating evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament or mishap one gets into.

clue.text: Open deception

definitions.meaning: a pretence intended to mislead, as in poker

explanation.surface: Deception carried out in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluff as an adjective means hearty and frank; as a noun it is a show of confidence meant to deceive.

clue.text: Surround is erected, say, once worker comes round

indicators.note: comes round means the worker insect encloses the other letters

parts.note: a bee is the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected sets the word upright, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which say also means

explanation.surface: A building is put up once a labourer has turned up on site.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'erected' turns a word upwards; 'say' is the usual signal for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: To besiege a place is to surround it with armed forces.

clue.text: Period of American dominance in behaviour

parts.note: US is America, and an age is a period, so a US age is an era of American dominance
age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A historian discusses an era when America shaped how the world behaved.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is a customary way of acting or treating something, its habitual practice.

clue.text: Someone giving themselves airs locally?

parts.note: airs are tunes, and a performer of traditional local music delivers them, rather than putting on airs

explanation.surface: Someone acting pompously in their home town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving themselves airs' suggests snobbery, but here airs are songs and locally points to folk tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of traditional songs of a region literally sings local airs.

clue.text: Subsequently beam, having ousted leader

indicators.note: having ousted leader means the first letter of the beam word is dropped

parts.note: a rafter is a roof beam

explanation.surface: A beam is in place only after its chief has been forced out.
explanation.definitionFit: After used as an adverb means later, at a following time.

clue.text: Stop, completely behind trees

indicators.note: behind places the word for completely after the word for trees

parts.note: a forest is a mass of trees
all can mean wholly, as in all alone

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt, hidden entirely behind a stand of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to prevent something by acting first, heading it off.

clue.text: Soldiers run from means of restraint

indicators.note: run from means the run letter is taken away from the restraint word

parts.note: a leg iron is a shackle
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Troops flee from their shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a large Roman army unit, hence a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Dickinson, say, US writer, literary heroine

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
Tess is the heroine of Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.surface: A list of American authors and a famous fictional heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Dickinson was a female poet, an example of the old word for a woman who writes verse.

clue.text: A firm mostly getting more working — one's looking up

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for firm is cut off

parts.note: strong means firm or solid

indicators.note: working signals that the letters of more are reworked

explanation.surface: A company gets more out of its staff, and its prospects improve.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer studies the stars and so spends the night gazing skywards.

clue.text: Seaman cracked his head cramming male …

indicators.note: cracked signals that the letters of his are broken up and rearranged
cramming means the head word is stuffed with the letter for male

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A sailor injured his head while squeezing past a man, the start of a naval story.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is a fellow sailor serving on the same vessel.

clue.text: … commander in hold, …

definitions.meaning: Admiral Lord ... led the British fleet at Trafalgar
a wrestling grip applied from behind the opponent's neck

explanation.surface: A leader in a grip, continuing the naval story.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson was Britain's most famous admiral; a nelson (full or half) is a wrestling hold.

clue.text: African region redeveloped as green site

indicators.note: redeveloped suggests a site rebuilt, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild area of Africa turned into a construction plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast plain in Tanzania famous for its wildlife.

clue.text: Indicator of North or South sailor observed below mast

indicators.note: in a down clue, observed below places the later pieces under the mast word

parts.note: a mast is a pole
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor at the foot of the mast looks for a guide to direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole star, Polaris, sits almost directly above the North Pole and shows where north lies.

clue.text: … commander that's organised gala in navy

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the navy abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: organised indicates the letters of gala are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A commander puts on a party aboard ship, ending the naval story.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Raglan commanded British forces in the Crimean War.

clue.text: Verdi opera about Egyptian god picked up in Stoppard play

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up lifts the pieces so they read upwards

parts.note: Aida is an opera by Verdi
C (circa) means about
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: An Italian opera with an Egyptian setting gets taken up in a modern English play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses AIDA C RA to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a 1993 play by Tom Stoppard.

clue.text: Start to lose name for primarily responsible dealing

indicators.note: to lose means the start word gives up one letter, which is swapped out

parts.note: to commence is to start

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of responsible

explanation.surface: Advice to begin dropping a person's name, as the one chiefly accountable for business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' says the R takes the place of the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is trade, the buying and selling of goods.

clue.text: Award involving one college examination

indicators.note: involving means the award word contains the other pieces

parts.note: a medal is an award
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A prize that comes with a single university test.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical check-up by a doctor.

clue.text: Lied about love? Not half — I'm leaving

indicators.note: about means the song word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song

indicators.note: Not half keeps only the first half of love

explanation.surface: Someone who lied about being in love, only half meaning it, walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lied' is the German song, not the past tense of lie.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal farewell, like goodbye.

clue.text: Backing some Caribbean company in Verdi opera

indicators.note: Backing turns the Caribbean word round so it reads in reverse

parts.note: a Cuban is one Caribbean person

explanation.surface: A Caribbean firm sponsors a production of an Italian opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabucco is Verdi's opera about King Nebuchadnezzar.

clue.text: Stock's rubbish — no successful item visible

definitions.note: stock as livestock, plural cattle; 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: no means the successful item is removed from the rubbish word

parts.note: bullshit is vulgar slang for nonsense
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A share is worthless, with no winning product in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' is cattle rather than shares, though bulls also suits the market surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock or cattle include male animals of the herd.

clue.text: Finish still to occur, not start

indicators.note: not start means the opening letter of the pending word is dropped

parts.note: pending means awaiting or yet to happen

explanation.surface: The end hasn't arrived yet, and nothing has begun either.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the conclusion or close of something.

clue.text: Pierce, producing blood

definitions.meaning: to stab with a horn or tusk
spilt, clotted blood from a wound

explanation.surface: A stab wound that draws blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull may gore a matador, piercing him; gore is also blood shed in violence.

clue.text: Inelegant start to Texan oil drama rubbished

indicators.note: rubbished suggests the letters are trashed and thrown into a new order
start to picks the first letter of Texan

explanation.surface: A critic pans the clumsy opening of a Texan oil soap opera, in the vein of Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means clumsy or lacking skill and grace.

clue.text: Conservative to start over ideology

parts.note: to redo is to do again from the beginning

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician begins again on the party's political philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs, a creed guiding someone's actions.

clue.text: Cheers after debut in role as Caribbean religionist

indicators.note: after places the thanks word at the end
debut in takes the first letter of role

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A toast after an actor's first appearance in a part as a Caribbean believer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian follows a Jamaican faith revering Haile Selassie.

clue.text: Girl's to eat after brewing lager

definitions.note: girl's here is girl is, a female name

indicators.note: brewing suggests the beer is being made, so its letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: A young woman is set to eat once she has brewed some beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraldine is a female given name.
